captured_item_bindings.exact_stem: A grid has grid-template-columns: repeat(3, 1fr) and grid-auto-flow: row (default sparse packing). Three children in document order: A (grid-column: span 2), B (grid-column: span 2), C (no placement rules). Which cell is left empty after all items are placed?
captured_item_bindings.exact_disputed_feedback: This would be true with grid-auto-flow: row dense, which allows the cursor to revisit earlier gaps. Default sparse packing skips the gap at row 1, col 3.

fixed_rules_preserved: Children A, B and C in that document order, with default order values.
A and B each have grid-column: span 2; C has no placement declaration.
Sparse case uses grid-auto-flow: row; dense case changes only that placement mode to row dense.
Neither case assigns explicit grid-row positions, additional placement, row spans, or different order values.

presentation_scaffolding.assessment: Makes the stem's stated grid concrete; it does not add a new placement condition.

Provide measurable 100-pixel columns and 40-pixel rows for the tiny A/B/C labels. These sizes do not change the number of columns, spans, item order, or sparse/dense placement search. They make the same logical occupancy observable; no claim is made about arbitrary content or size-dependent CSS not present here.

presentation_scaffolding.assessment: Affect location and measurement convenience, not the declared grid placement. Each rectangle is measured relative to its own container origin.

native_measurement_binding.observed_values_come_from: The agent-owned JavaScript calls getBoundingClientRect on the actual grid and its actual children. It reports measured width/height and derives row, column and span from offsets divided by the declared row/column dimensions. It does not return stored expected placements or a hard-coded success verdict.
native_measurement_binding.row_and_column_interpretation: The fixed local document has ordinary horizontal left-to-right defaults and no contrary writing-mode or direction rule. This is one legitimate concrete realization of the logical grid problem.
native_measurement_binding.grids_have_two_rows: Observed height 80 with fixed 40-pixel rows establishes two rendered rows; the explicit template establishes three columns.

finding.reason: Each run occupies five cells in a two-row, three-column grid. Dense packing moves C into the earlier gap and leaves the later cell empty. The native observation corroborates that No cell is left empty remains false under row dense.
